newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon minister says new IMF deal imminent.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon minister says new IMF deal imminent.

text.p: Cameroon's finance minister has said a delegation from the International Monetary Fund will visit soon to finalise an agreement on an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility.

In remarks to the GICAM employers' association reported by state media, Edouard Akame M'foumou said the three-year accord was expected to go before the IMF board for approval in the second half of July.

Speaking on Friday, he said the IMF's demands for an increase in the price of oil products, liberalisation of shipping, and restructuring of local bank Credit Agricole du Cameroun would be met in time for the accord to be signed.
He gave no details on how much Cameroon hoped to received under the accord.
One government source said the delegation was expected to arrive on June 8.
Previous IMF accords with Cameroon have run into trouble because of non-fulfilment of terms. The third and fourth tranches of a standby accord which expired last year were not released.
